title: Paper 1 style section (25 marks)
subject: Computing
source: Written for computing/y11 lesson 36 (Pupil PDF worksheet: 25-mark Paper 1 style section (mark scheme in the plan))
intro: Lesson 36. Data, hardware, networks and security. About 1.5 minutes a mark; answer what you know first; leave time to check.

questions.q: State one reason programmers use hexadecimal.
questions.a: It is shorter and easier to read than binary, so fewer mistakes

questions.q: A mono sound is recorded for 30 seconds at 22,050 Hz with a bit depth of 8 bits. Calculate its size in bytes.
Explain the role of the program counter in the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
questions.a: It holds the address of the next instruction (1); it is incremented after each fetch so instructions run in sequence (1)

questions.q: Give two differences between RAM and secondary storage.
questions.a: RAM is volatile, secondary storage is not (1); RAM is faster but smaller in capacity (1)

questions.q: A 12,000,000-bit file is sent over a 3,000,000 bits per second link. Calculate the time taken.
Describe how TCP and IP work together to send data across the internet.
questions.a: TCP splits the data into numbered packets (1); IP addresses each packet and routes it across the network, possibly by different routes (1); TCP reassembles the packets in order and asks for any missing ones (1)

questions.q: Explain how a firewall protects a network.
questions.a: It checks incoming and outgoing traffic against rules (1) and blocks traffic that is not allowed, such as unauthorised access (1)

questions.q: Describe one way phishing tricks users and one way to protect against it.
questions.a: A message pretends to be from a trusted organisation (1) asking the user to click a link and enter details (1); protection: check the sender and link, never enter passwords from an email link, staff training, email filters (1)

questions.q: A school plans to store pupils' records in the cloud. Discuss the impact of this decision.
questions.a: Level 3 (5-6): a balanced discussion with a conclusion. Points: access from anywhere and automatic backups; no servers to maintain; but depends on the internet; privacy and security of personal data; data protection law (the school stays responsible); cost of subscriptions; where the data is stored.
